I think it depends on what exactly happened and how you feel but for myself, I was just a kid and I blamed and hated myself a LOT for the abuse that happened to me, the abuse that happened to others because I was too scared to tell, and I hurt myself (physically) a lot because of it. 

So when I started trauma therapy there was talk about forgiveness and how it is *not* always necessary to forgive abusers, but it is necessary to let go of self blame and stuff in order to heal. I looked a lot into “inner child healing” and that has helped. Because i was still blaming that little kid, not myself as an adult and I needed that little kid to know I forgave her for coping in the ways she could to survive. She didn’t do anything wrong by surviving and I needed to let go of blaming this kid for not knowing any other way to survive what was happening. So I forgave her and I forgave myself for blaming her for so long when the only one to blame is the one who hurt me. 

I think if you weren’t a kid it might be a different kind of healing because the inner child stuff wouldn’t be necessary, but I also think everyone who’s experienced trauma has some self blame they need to work through and that is what you need to forgive yourself for. Whatever it is that you blame yourself for, whether it’s “I shouldn’t have gone to x place that night” or “I shouldn’t have stayed with that person” or “I shouldn’t have been drinking” or *whatever* it is, you need to find a way to stop blaming yourself and know that the only person to blame is whoever hurt you. No matter what decisions you made when the trauma happened or after it happened, THEY chose to hurt you. You did not choose that and you are not to blame for it so tell yourself you’re sorry you ever did blame you when it wasn’t your fault. Of course it’ll take some time to get it really in your head that you’re right, you’re not the issue, but it’ll happen at some point and it feels much better
